Swiggy competes primarily with [[Zomato]] in food delivery.{{cite web |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/companies/online-food-delivery-wars-are-moving-from-india-to-bharat/articleshow/68447011.cms |title=Online food delivery wars are moving from India to Bharat |newspaper=[[The Times of India]] |date= 17 March 2019|author= Madhav Chanchani|access-date= 13 August 2019}} In quick-commerce, Instamart ranks behind competitors [[Blinkit]] and [[Zepto (company)|Zepto]] in terms of market share.{{cite news |title=India - Internet Sector Research Report (16 June 2025) |url=https://jmflresearch.com/JMnew/JMCRM/analystreports/pdf/QC_Sector_Update_16062025.pdf |access-date=30 November 2025 |work=[[JM Financial]]}}{{cite news |title=Zepto surpasses Swiggy Instamart in daily orders, closes in on Blinkit |url=https://www.financialexpress.com/business/start-ups/zepto-surpasses-swiggy-instamart-in-daily-orders-closes-in-on-blinkit/3834689/ |access-date=30 November 2025 |work=Financial Express}} == History == In 2013, Sriharsha Majety and Nandan Reddy designed an [[e-commerce]] website called Bundl to facilitate courier service and shipping within India.{{cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/Companies/NsVFwJMvONZm8qEDJuGoOM/How-Swiggy-became-Indias-fastest-unicorn.html|title=How Swiggy Became India's Fastest Unicorn|date=27 June 2018|work=Livemint|access-date=31 August 2019}} Bundl was halted in 2014 and rebranded to enter the food delivery market.{{cite web|url=https://www.entrepreneur.com/article/325292|title=Swiggy Timeline: From a Bootstrapped Venture to India's Fastest Growing Unicorn (Infographic)|date=23 December 2018|work=Entrepreneur|access-date=31 August 2019}} Majety and Reddy approached Rahul Jaimini, formerly with [[Myntra]], and launched Swiggy in August 2014.{{cite news |last1=Kanth |first1=K. Rajani |title=A start-up by IIM, IIT grads to quickly deliver food from restaurants! |url=https://www.rediff.com/business/report/pix-special-start-up-by-iim-iit-grads-to-quickly-deliver-food-from-restaurants/20150707.htm |access-date=27 February 2023 |work=Rediff |language=en}} By 2015, Swiggy expanded its food delivery operations from just Bengaluru to eight [[Classification of Indian cities|Tier 1 cities]] across India.{{cite news |title=Bengaluru's food delivery start-up Swiggy expands operations to Pune |url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/bengalurus-food-delivery-start-up-swiggy-expands-operations-to-pune/articleshow/48158976.cms |access-date=2 April 2024 |work=The Economic Times |date=21 July 2015}}{{cite news |title=Online food ordering platform Swiggy raises $7 mn |url=https://www.techcircle.in/2016/05/10/online-food-ordering-platform-swiggy-raises-7-mn |access-date=2 April 2024 |work=Techcircle |date=10 May 2016 |language=en}} At the time, the food delivery sector was in turmoil as several notable startups, such as [[Foodpanda]] (later acquired by [[Ola Cabs]]), TinyOwl (later acquired by [[Zomato]]) and Ola Cafe (later closed) were struggling. In January 2017, Swiggy started its [[cloud kitchen]] chain called "The Bowl Company".{{cite news |title=Swiggy sets up cloud kitchen 'The Bowl Company' in Bengaluru |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/startups/companies/swiggy-sets-up-cloud-kitchen-the-bowl-company-in-bengaluru/articleshow/56659238.cms |access-date=27 February 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=19 January 2017}} In November 2017, Swiggy started a [[kitchen incubator]] business called Swiggy Access, opening a network of ready-to-occupy kitchens for its restaurant partners.{{cite news |title=Swiggy launches ready-to-occupy kitchens 'Swiggy Access' |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/business/india-business/swiggy-launches-ready-to-occupy-kitchens-swiggy-access/articleshow/61642315.cms |access-date=27 February 2023 |work=The Times of India |date=14 November 2017}} By 2019, over 1,000 Swiggy Access kitchens were operational, according to a ''[[TechCrunch]]'' report.{{cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Manish |title=India's Swiggy bets big on cloud kitchens |url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/11/19/swiggy-cloud-kitchen-india/ |access-date=27 February 2023 |work=TechCrunch |date=20 November 2019}} In mid-2018, Swiggy was operational in 16 Indian cities,{{cite news |last1=Bansal |first1=Varsha |title=Food delivery fight grips small-town India |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/start-ups/food-delivery-fight-grips-small-town-india-1562002126818.html |access-date=2 April 2024 |work=mint |date=1 July 2019 |language=en}} which increased to 500 cities in 2019, matching the scale of rival [[Zomato]].{{cite news |title=Swiggy now in 500 Indian cities, targets 100 more this year |url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/swiggy-now-in-500-indian-cities-targets-100-more-this-year-11570435306526.html |access-date=2 April 2024 |work=mint |date=7 October 2019 |language=en}} In Swiggy goes beyond food to offer product delivery from local stores |website=[[TechCrunch]] |date= February 2019|author= Jon Russell|access-date= 13 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=https://www.theweek.in/theweek/business/2019/04/26/how-food-aggregator-apps-like-swiggy-zomato-are-trying-innovative-business-methods.html |title=How food aggregator apps like Swiggy, Zomato, are trying innovative business methods |newspaper=[[The Week (Indian magazine)|The Week]] |date= 27 April 2019 |author= Abhinav Singh|access-date= 13 August 2019}}{{cite web|author=Deepti (magazine)|Fortune]]}} In September 2019, Swiggy launched Swiggy Go, a [[package delivery]] service.{{Cite web|url=https://techcrunch.com/2019/09/04/swiggy-delivery-anything-dunzo/|title=India's Swiggy has a new service that will deliver just about anything|website=TechCrunch|date=4 September 2019 |access-date=2 March 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.livemint.com/companies/news/swiggy-launches-instant-pick-up-and-drop-service-swiggy-go-1567582575602.html|title=Swiggy launches instant pick up and drop service 'Swiggy Go'|date=4 September 2019|website=Livemint}} In April 2020, it rebranded Swiggy Go as Swiggy Genie.{{cite news |last1=Singh |first1=Jitendra |title=Swiggy expands grocery delivery service to more cities; rebrands Swiggy Go |url=https://entrackr.com/2020/04/swiggy-expands-its-grocery-delivery-service-to-more-cities |access-date=25 January 2022 |work=Entrackr |date=9 April 2020}} During the [[COVID-19 off 1,100 employees during the pandemic.{{cite news|url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/small-biz/startups/newsbuzz/swiggy-sacks-1100-employees-as-covid-19-derails-cloud-kitchens/articleshow/75801555.cms|title=Swiggy lays off 1,100 employees extract:
Swiggy Limited is an Indian online food ordering and delivery company, headquartered in Bengaluru. As of 2025, it operates food delivery services in more than 700 Indian cities, and quick-commerce services under the name Instamart in 100 cities. The company was incorporated in 2013.
Swiggy competes primarily with Zomato in food delivery. In quick-commerce, Instamart ranks behind competitors Blinkit and Zepto in terms of market share.
